facts.fact: Founded in 1989 by a crew of Vancouver, Canada-based climbers; started as a basement operation making climbing harnesses and packs.
Originally named Rock Solid by co-founder Dave Lane; in 1990 Lane sold his stake to Blair Murdoch, Tim Duholke and Jeremy Guard, and the company was renamed Arc'teryx in 1991.
The name and bird logo reference the Archaeopteryx fossil; the brand is colloquially called 'dead bird'.
Its first breakout product was the thermolaminated Vapor harness; Gore-Tex technical apparel followed in 1996.
Headquartered in North Vancouver, B.C.; designs and tests gear in the Coast Mountains of British Columbia, which the brand calls its proving ground.
Known for Gore-Tex shell jackets and technical mountain apparel; also runs ReBIRD (wash, repair, trade-in, resale) to extend the life of its gear.
Owned by Amer Sports since 2005 (Salomon Group before that, from 2001).

quotes.quote: Obsessively designed gear for mountain athletes.
Every piece we make serves a purpose and solves a problem for mountain athletes, delivering functionality, simplicity, and durability in a timeless design.

products.golf_note: A 9" inseam reads as a normal course short. The stretch nylon has a water-repellent finish and zip pockets keep a ball marker and keys from walking off between shots. Best for warm Austin days the rest of the year.

products.golf_note: A thin, warm quarter-zip that looks right on a first tee. The smooth fleece face is built for durability, and the deep zip lets you dump heat as the morning warms up.
